thought.text:
**Diagnosis:** In `parse_unquoted_value` (parser.py:123-125), the regex `\s+#.*` requires whitespace before `#`, so `KEY= # explanation` yields `part = " # explanation"`; the substitution matches and strips to `""`... but wait — the value regex `_unquoted_value` is `([^\r\n]*)`, which consumes the whole rest of line including the comment. The `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part)` then removes it, giving `""`. So the empty case should already work — unless the issue is that `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) consumes the space, leaving `part = "# explanation"` with no preceding whitespace, so `\s+#` doesn't match and the value becomes `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

**Change plan:** Fix `parse_unquoted_value` to treat a `#` at the start of the (post-`=`) remainder as a comment: change the strip regex to `(?:^|\s+)#.*` (or `re.sub(r"(^|\s+)#.*", "", part)`), then `.rstrip()`. This keeps `KEY=#literal` and `KEY=a#b` literal (no preceding whitespace), preserves quoting/exports/ordinary comments, and makes `KEY= # explanation` → `""`. Add parser tests for these three cases.

action.message:
**Diagnosis:** `parse_unquoted_value` (parser.py:123-125) strips comments with `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part)`, which requires whitespace before `#`. But `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) already consumes the space after `=`, so for `KEY= # explanation` the remainder is `"# explanation"` — no preceding whitespace — so the comment isn't stripped and the value becomes `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

**Change plan:** In `parse_unquoted_value`, change the strip regex to also match a `#` at the start of the remainder, e.g. `re.sub(r"(?:^|\s+)#.*", "", part).rstrip()`. This makes `KEY= # explanation` → `""`, while `KEY=#literal` and `KEY=a#b` stay literal (no preceding whitespace), and quoting/exports/ordinary comments are untouched. Add parser tests covering these three cases.
